title: Whole f45r Q2: latest ordinary mention changes the final DAL reference
summary: EXPLORATORY SAME-PASSAGE ALTERNATIVE. Keep Q1 grouping, ordered entries and functional paragraph fields. Resolve each field descriptor to the latest earlier ordinary exact occurrence on this page, including the current paragraph. DALDY/DALOR then refer to f45r.6G007, while final DALDAIIN refers to f45r.10G009. No meanings assigned.

design.phase: exploratory reconstruction after target inspection, not a fixed prediction
design.retained: All86raw groups,61ordered positions27/17/17,15field descriptions,5free markers,5finite compounds,one field value per marker/paragraph. Whole descriptions remain untranslated. Use only Q1 grouping and ordinary position definitions, never its identities.

types.position: One ordered specification position per ordinary occurrence. Distinct positions are part of the proposed content, not merely saved source addresses.
types.referent: Each position has a referent; two positions may denote the same real entity. No physical distinctness, portion, action or time asserted.
types.description: The same unknown predicate N_w constrains both ordinary referents and field arguments.
types.field: Single value per marker per textual paragraph record, not per described object.

reference_rule: Read all events in written source order on this page. An ordinary entry introduces a position and referent described by its exact whole form; it becomes the latest eligible mention of that descriptor.

At a field event, only earlier ordinary entries with exactly the same descriptor are candidates. Current-paragraph ordinary entries are allowed. Select the most recent source position; with none, retain an unanchored argument.
A field occurrence or successful reprise does not update the latest-ordinary table. Embedded substrings, inferred properties and future occurrences never enter the search.
Fix the chosen source anchor at the field event. Do not later recompute it when a new ordinary occurrence arrives.

Unify descriptions/anchors of the same functional paragraph field. This may resolve an earlier open variable after a later explicit anchor. It does not retrospectively choose an anchor for an earlier event.
If two explicit anchors constrain one field, retain their referent equality obligation; do not silently discard one. Distinct source positions do not establish distinct physical referents.
changed_from_q1: allow earlier ordinary occurrences in the current paragraph
choose last eligible occurrence rather than requiring a single candidate
design.predicted_authored_consequence: Of four reprises only final DALDAIIN changes anchor: KOL and DOR constrain the older DAL(.6G007), opaque OTYDAL the later DAL(.10G009). DAIN(.9G004) cannot retroactively anchor DAIN CTHEY(.8).
design.order_limit: Moving DALDAIIN across the later ordinary DAL can change its target. Moving it only within the later interval, or swapping DALDY/DALOR before that DAL, need not. Exact paragraph-final position is not explained.
design.meaning_limit: Chosen after seeing this sequence; no independent prediction, word value, physical process, object inequality or empirical superiority. Positive unknown descriptors remain flexible. Q1/R1 are frozen separate alternatives.

decision_note.known: Stable exact OPCHAL/DAL occurrences, source order, finite free/bound hypothesis and full Q1 accounting. Q1 excludes current-paragraph candidates and leaves final DALDAIIN placement inert.
decision_note.unknown: Whether a human writer intended ordinary mentions to refresh reference while field forms reuse it. The actual late DAL permits a concrete order-dependent consequence, not merely another arbitrary dictionary.
